ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, one can see a smooth closed polar curve on the coordinate axes, with a shape similar to a slightly downward-bulging limacon, with no inner loop and no separated parts, so the entire closed region can be traced once by one complete period. The curve given in the problem is r = 3 - \sin\theta. Since the range of values of \sin\theta is [-1,1], the range of values of r = 3 - \sin\theta is [2,4], always positive; at the same time, the period of this function is 2\pi. Therefore take \theta from 0 to 2\pi. The polar coordinate area formula is A = \frac12\int r^2\,d\theta. Substituting r = 3 - \sin\theta gives the area expression \frac12\int_0^{2\pi}(3-\sin\theta)^2\,d\theta.

raw_record.question_text: For the polar curve $r = 3 - \sin \theta$, what integral expression gives the area of the region enclosed by the curve?

method.method_draft: First read the image as showing one smooth, closed polar curve on coordinate axes, with no inner loop or separate component, so the enclosed region is traced once over a full polar period. From the text, use the curve equation r = 3 - sin(theta). Since 3 - sin(theta) is always positive and has period 2pi, take theta from 0 to 2pi. Apply the standard polar area formula A = 1/2 integral r^2 dtheta, giving A = 1/2 integral_0^{2pi} (3 - sin(theta))^2 dtheta.

From the text, set x = (3 - sin(theta))cos(theta) and y = (3 - sin(theta))sin(theta). Use the Cartesian line-integral area formula A = 1/2 integral (x dy - y dx) around the closed curve.
